query: How does resolution time vary across category, priority, and assignment group?

per_column.name: incident_category
per_column.rationale: Well-separated, interpretable categories (email, database, vpn, etc.) that can be grouped and compared against resolution time; a strong external segmentation variable.

per_column.name: affected_system
per_column.rationale: Interpretable, reasonably balanced categories of the affected system; supports meaningful comparison of resolution time across systems.

per_column.name: failure_symptom
per_column.rationale: Clear symptom categories (connection_failure, outage_down, access_denied...) that are external and can be segmented against resolution time.

per_column.name: scope_qualifier
per_column.rationale: Interpretable scope categories (general, remote_access, location_specific...); usable for grouping, though somewhat dominated by 'general'.

per_column.name: resolver_match
per_column.rationale: Boolean whether resolver matched assignee; interpretable segmentation that could relate to resolution time, though 100 NULLs weaken it.

per_column.name: assignment_lag_present
per_column.rationale: Interpretable boolean about assignment lag; a plausible associational variable, though heavily skewed (428 true vs 72 false).

per_column.name: caller_id_group
per_column.rationale: Named 'group' but values are individual caller identities; high-cardinality identifier that is essentially a restatement of caller_id, not a meaningful segmentation.

per_column.name: resolution_delay_proxy
per_column.rationale: Bins based directly on resolution time (same_day, over_seven_days, unresolved); this restates the focus variable rather than providing an external relationship.

judge.rationale: Most added columns are genuine external, interpretable segmentation variables (incident_category, affected_system, failure_symptom, scope_qualifier, resolver_match, assignment_lag_present) that let a human group and compare resolution time. Two columns weaken the set: resolution_delay_proxy is a direct restatement/binning of the focus, and caller_id_group is a high-cardinality identifier rather than a segmentation. Some predictors are also skewed (scope_qualifier, assignment_lag_present) reducing comparative power, but as a set they still support meaningful exploratory relationships with the focus.
